inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand. Visibility is below 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi until 18:00 today, 16 Feb. Visibility can drop suddenly.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust and low visibility in coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi until 18:00
fields.instruction: Drive with caution, especially on external and open roads, and be ready for sudden drops in visibility. Updates: https://alerts.example.ae
fields.note_for_reviewer: The source gives 10:30 to 18:00 without a time zone, so I assumed local UAE time and kept '18:00 today, 16 Feb'. The source says visibility is below 3,000 m only in 'some' areas, not across the whole demo zone, and I rated severity as Moderate based on that; please confirm both.

versions.description: تمرين - رياح شمالية غربية قوية تثير الغبار والرمال. مدى الرؤية أقل من 3,000 م في بعض المناطق الساحلية والداخلية من أبوظبي حتى الساعة 18:00 اليوم، 16 فبراير. قد ينخفض مدى الرؤية بشكل مفاجئ.
versions.headline: تمرين: غبار متطاير وانخفاض في مدى الرؤية في المناطق الساحلية والداخلية من أبوظبي حتى الساعة 18:00
versions.instruction: قُد بحذر، خاصة على الطرق الخارجية والمفتوحة، وكن مستعداً لانخفاض مفاجئ في مدى الرؤية. التحديثات: https://alerts.example.ae

objections.issue: Wind strength is overstated. The bulletin describes winds as 'active to occasionally strong', but the alert says simply 'Strong northwesterly winds'.

objections.fix: Remove 'of Abu Dhabi' from the headline and description and use the bulletin's wording 'some coastal and inland areas' (or name the areas explicitly, if NCM gives them).
objections.issue: The affected area does not match the bulletin. NCM (a national centre) warns of 'some coastal and inland areas' without naming an emirate; 'ABU DHABI' is only the WAM dateline. The alert limits the hazard to 'coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi', which the bulletin does not support and which may leave out affected areas elsewhere.

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin on hazard, visibility (below 3,000 m) and end time (18:00). Two details go beyond the bulletin. The wind is overstated as plain 'strong'. The affected areas are narrowed to 'Abu Dhabi', which the bulletin does not say. Both can be fixed by the drafter.

no_basis.concern: The console is in the live environment and the drill is addressed with scope Public. On live UAE-Alert cell broadcast, an Exercise-status message may still reach handsets on the exercise channel. Whether a public exercise on the live system is authorised for this drill is a decision for the people approving it; no clause shown forbids it.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring exercise or drill alerts on a live console to use a restricted scope, or prohibiting public Exercise broadcasts without prior notice.

The alert is an initial Alert with no references, which is correct. There are no active alerts from other authorities that it could overreach.

no_basis.concern: No clause shown to me specifically requires the protective action to appear on the first page, as opposed to anywhere in the message. The first-page placement in my fix rests on my mandate rather than on a quoted clause.

For example, in English: 'Drive slowly, use low-beam lights, keep your distance; people with breathing problems stay indoors.' Add an equivalent in Arabic placed early in the text. Keep both languages well under 15 pages.
objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text tells people what to do. Both describe the hazard (dust, sand, visibility below 3,000 m) and then stop, ending with a statement about the hazard. There is no protective action, so the first page does not carry hazard and action together.

payload.summary: The Arabic matches the English in meaning across the headline, description and instruction. The exercise label (تمرين) is present. The hazard matches: northwesterly winds raising dust and sand, low visibility. The figures match: below 3,000 m, until 18:00 today, 16 Feb. The places match: coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi. left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was excluded on verification grounds.

The suggested advice 'people with breathing problems stay indoors' was not used. The NCM bulletin does not mention a health risk, so adding it would introduce a hazard that is not in the verified inputs.

The suggested 'use low-beam lights' and 'keep your distance' were not used. The bulletin's only advice is to exercise caution when driving on external and open roads, so the instruction stays close to that wording.
'Abu Dhabi' was removed as the area name. In the bulletin it is only the WAM dateline; NCM says 'some coastal and inland areas' without naming an emirate.
An Arabic version was not drafted here because this output is English only. The Arabic phone text needs the same fixes: hazard and protective action on the first page, and no limit to Abu Dhabi.
fields.note_for_reviewer: The bulletin gives 18:00 without a timezone or date, so I assumed UAE local time on 16 Feb 2026. Please also confirm whether the operator's demo target area should still be described as 'Abu Dhabi' in the area polygon now that the text follows NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas'.

payload.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin in every point I check. The hazard is the same: northwesterly winds raising dust and sand. Visibility is under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas, and conditions run until 18:00 on 16 Feb. Severity Moderate fits a caution-level warning. Certainty Observed fits because conditions began at 10:30 and are ongoing. Urgency Immediate fits. Every input used is verified, and the Exercise status is clearly marked. The alert leaves out the 10:30 start time, but that is not a misstatement.

no_basis.concern: This Exercise alert has scope Public and is being prepared on a console whose environment is 'live'. If it is broadcast, real members of the public could receive drill traffic. Approvers should confirm that a public-reaching exercise from the live console is intended. None of the clauses shown sets a rule on exercise messages with Public scope from a live environment.
no_basis.searched_for: Rules restricting CAP status Exercise with scope Public, or exercise transmission from live or production consoles, in the CAP, CAP-AU, CAP-CP, ETSI EU-Alert and NCEMA clauses returned.

payload.summary: The sender is in the issuer register at level 1, with all areas and categories allowed. The alert's area description and codes match the area requested for the uae-dust-drill event. Status is Exercise, which fits the EXERCISE / DRILL context, and the headline is prefixed EXERCISE. No active alerts from other authorities exist, so there is nothing to overreach. msgType is Alert, so no reference to an earlier alert is needed. Nothing within my mandate is wrong.

no_basis.concern: The first page does not carry the action in either language. English (GSM-7, about 93 characters a page) breaks page 1 around 'strong northwesterly winds are raisin…', and 'Drive with caution' is on page 3. Arabic (UCS-2, 41 characters a page) has only 'تمرين - ليس تنبيهاً حقيقياً. NCM: رياح شمالية' on page 1, and the action 'قُد بحذر' is on page 6. Handsets that show only the first page, or users who read only that far, would miss the action. The drafter could shorten the text or move the hazard and the action up front, for example 'EXERCISE - NOT A REAL ALERT. Dust/sand, visibility under 3,000 m until 18:00. Drive with caution…'.
no_basis.searched_for: A TDRA TS FS 001, TS040 or 3GPP TS 23.041 clause requiring that the first cell broadcast page contain the hazard and the protective action. The returned clauses cover language support, encoding, page parameter coding and the 'immediately recognizable' requirement, but none sets first-page content.

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Both are within the 15-page cell broadcast maximum: English is 3 pages and Arabic is 6. The encodings are correct: GSM-7 for English and UCS-2 for Arabic, as 3GPP TS 23.038 requires for Arabic. The exercise marker opens both texts. The multi-page length is already recorded as gap G6. One concern has no supporting clause: the protective action ('Drive with caution') falls on the last page, not the first, in both languages. It is listed under no_basis for the drafter and approvers to consider.

no_basis.concern: The agency abbreviation 'NCM' is left in Latin script in the Arabic description, and Arabic readers may not recognise it. The Arabic name (المركز الوطني للأرصاد) could be used instead. This is a matter of style and clarity, not a difference in meaning.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring agency names or acronyms to be localised in Arabic alert text
